body:
**Minervini SEPA and the Trend Template (*Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard*, 2013)**
- The Trend Template (as published by Minervini; online lists vary slightly):
  1. Price above both the 150-day and 200-day MA.
  2. 150-day MA above the 200-day MA.
  3. 200-day MA trending up for at least 1 month (preferably 4-5 months).
  4. 50-day MA above both the 150-day and 200-day MA.
  5. Price above the 50-day MA.
  6. Price at least 30% above its 52-week low (some lists say 25%).
  7. Price within 25% of its 52-week high (closer is better).
  8. IBD RS rating at least 70 (preferably 80s-90s).
  — [Chartmill: SEPA explained](https://www.chartmill.com/documentation/trading-and-investing/methodologies/523-SEPA-Explained-Mark-Minervinis-Specific-Entry-Point-Analysis-System) [F]; [Sharpely: Minervini trend template for Stage 2 stocks](https://sharpely.in/blogs/minervini-trend-template-for-stage-2-stocks/) [F]; [Deepvue: Trend Template](https://deepvue.com/?p=3926) [F]. Discrepancy: some implementations use 25% vs 30% above the low, or drop the 52-week-low check; one scanner counts 7 criteria. The template is a universe filter, not an entry signal.
- SEPA's 5 elements (per Minervini): Trend (Stage 2 via Trend Template), Fundamentals (earnings/sales growth, ideally accelerating; earnings surprises/estimate revisions), Catalyst, Entry points (low-risk pivot, usually VCP), Exits (predefined stop and sell rules). — [Chartmill SEPA](https://www.chartmill.com/documentation/trading-and-investing/methodologies/523-SEPA-Explained-Mark-Minervinis-Specific-Entry-Point-Analysis-System) [F]
- Volatility Contraction Pattern (VCP): a base with 2-6 successive pullbacks ("T"s), each roughly half the depth of the prior (e.g., 25% -> 12% -> 6% -> 3%), volume drying up into the right side; buy the pivot (high of the final tight contraction) on expanding volume. Stop typically just below the last contraction low; Minervini's maximum stop is 10%, average loss targeted around 5-6% or less, and he says to keep average win larger than average loss by about 2-3x. [K] — book; summarized at [Chartmill SEPA](https://www.chartmill.com/documentation/trading-and-investing/methodologies/523-SEPA-Explained-Mark-Minervinis-Specific-Entry-Point-Analysis-System)
- Minervini's verified US Investing Championship record: he won the 1997 USIC with a 155% return and has competed since. — [USIC press (BusinessWire, 2023)](https://businesswire.com/news/home/20230125005300/en/United-States-Investing-Championship-2022-Final-Standings) [F] for participation; 155%/1997 is [K].

`insight:auditor-exit-signal` | 2026-11-19 | tickers: - | confidence: verified

Auditor exits and delayed audited results preceded or accompanied many collapses: Reliance Capital & Reliance Home Finance (PwC resigned 2019 citing unresolved concerns), Byju's (Deloitte Jun 2023, BDO Sep 2024; FY21 accounts ~18 months late), Ricoh India (Q2FY16 results delayed after auditor queries), Jet Airways (Q1FY19 results deferred Aug 2018), Wirecard (KPMG special audit could not verify; EY refused 2019 sign-off), Credit Suisse (material weaknesses Mar 2023), Gensol/Brightcom (already in memory). In India, after the 2018-19 wave of mid-term auditor resignations, SEBI (Oct 2019) required auditors who resign to complete the quarter's limited review and disclose detailed reasons, which are filed on exchanges -- read them. Rules: (1) mid-term resignation with stated concerns (information not provided, fund diversion, going concern) = exit; (2) 'pre-occupation' or fee-related reasons from a large firm replaced by a tiny firm = strong flag; (3) delayed results beyond the regulatory deadline, or repeated qualified opinions/emphasis of matter on related-party balances = flag; (4) CFO resignation within months of auditor change compounds the signal. Auditor sign-off is weak evidence of honesty (Satyam/PwC, Wirecard/EY), but auditor exit is strong evidence of trouble.

**Links:** part_of -> `insight:disqualifiers`
**Sources:** <https://theprint.in/india/byjus-auditor-deloitte-three-board-members-sever-ties-with-embattled-edtech-startup/1638279/> ; <https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/ricoh-india-admits-accounting-violations-falsification-of-books-116071901198_1.html> ; <https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wirecard_scandal>

`event:india-crash-2008` | confidence: **verified** | tags: india, blowup, base-rate, smallcap, cyclical

Sensex 21,206.77 (10 Jan 2008) to a closing low of ~8,160 (9 Mar 2009), -61.5%; intraday it touched ~7,700 on 27 Oct 2008 (from memory). Nifty 50 TRI -59% (calendar 2008); Nifty Smallcap 250 TRI -73%; Nifty Smallcap 100 intra-year fall -76%; the BSE Smallcap was -70.7% from its 52-week high by 17 Oct 2008. Sensex P/E more than halved, ~27x to ~11.9x (Business Standard; Morningstar says ~12). What led the fall: realty (DLF, Unitech -90%+), infra, capital goods, metals, small caps; what held up relatively: FMCG, pharma, IT. Bottom signals: P/E ~11-12x, record FII selling, IPO market shut, dividend yields ~2%, policy response (RBI rate cuts from Oct 2008, fiscal stimulus) and the May 2009 election result (Sensex upper circuit on 18 May 2009). Recovery: Sensex regained ~21,000 in Nov 2010 (about 34 months from peak) but did not sustain new highs until late 2013; the Nifty Smallcap 100 took ~69 months (Nov 2014, Value Research) and the BSE Smallcap until ~2017 to close above its Jan 2008 high; Smallcap 250 TRI >6 years (DSP). Entry before the crisis gave ~8% CAGR to Mar 2026 in Smallcap 250 TRI vs ~18% from the bottom. Lesson: buying small caps at cycle-peak valuations can cost 6+ years even when the long-run trend is up.

`insight:regulator-outcomes-vs-conduct` · confidence: verified

Legal outcomes are poor proxies for how a promoter behaved, in both directions. Penalties quashed on appeal: SAT set aside SEBI's 2021 RPL manipulation penalty on Mukesh Ambani (Dec-2023) and a Rs 25 cr takeover penalty on the Ambani family (Jul-2023), citing SEBI's long delay; SAT quashed SEBI's 2021 insider-trading ban on Kishore Biyani (Dec-2023), even as Future Retail went into liquidation; the Supreme Court (Apr-2022) set aside insider-trading orders against PC Jeweller relatives. Settlements: Adani's MPS case was settled for ~Rs 1.48 cr (Sep-2026, no admission); the Sandesaras' criminal cases were quashed on a Rs 5,100 cr deposit (SC, Nov-2025), and the SC then told SEBI to close its case (2026). Dismissals: US DOJ charges against the Adanis were dismissed with prejudice (Aug-2026); SEBI found no violation on Hindenburg's related-party allegations (Sep-2025). Delay: Videocon-ICICI (FIR 2019), DHFL (CBI 2022), Yes Bank (2020) and Religare (2019) had no final criminal verdicts by Nov-2026; promoters got bail citing trial delay. Meanwhile, conduct is often visible directly in filings: ICDs to shells, collateral given for group debt, pledge cycles, auditor exits. Rules: (1) record regulator findings, interim orders, settlements and allegations as separate categories, which this library does; (2) a quashed penalty is not proof of good conduct, and an allegation is not proof of bad conduct; (3) for investing, the question is whether minority value was transferred, which filings can usually answer before the courts do.

Sources: <https://www.taxmann.com/post/blog/sat-quashes-sebis-order-imposing-penalty-on-mukesh-ambani-2-others-in-case-related-to-manipulative-trading/> · <https://www.outlookbusiness.com/news/sat-quashes-sebis-order-against-kishore-biyani-others-in-insider-trading-case> · <https://www.taxmann.com/post/blog/sc-sets-aside-insider-trading-orders-against-p-chand-jeweller/> · <https://www.moneylife.in/article/sebi-clears-vinod-adani-in-mps-case-gautam-adani-4-group-companies-settle-for-148-crore/81785.html> · <https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/economy/story/supreme-court-agrees-to-drop-criminal-proceedings-against-fugitive-sandesara-brothers-if-they-paid-rs-5100-crore-503463-2025-11-24>

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:US-UNH:2027-initial-eps-guide-22-50`
- **Method:** management-tone-vs-delivery · **P(ours)** 0.42 · **P(base)** 0.50 · resolve by 2027-01-31
- **Evidence:** 8-K 13-Oct-2026 (Q3 2026): revenue $112.7B; adjusted EPS $4.69; full-year 2026 outlook raised to net EPS 'at least $19.50' and adjusted EPS 'at least $20.50'; CEO cites 'discipline and execution'. Context: UNH opened 2026 with an 'at least' style floor well below where it now stands (post-2025 reset), i.e., deliberately conservative guidance.
- **Why our number differs from base:** Management-tone test: post-crisis UNH under-promises; an initial 2027 floor ≥$22.50 (≈+10% on the 2026 floor) would break that habit. Medicare Advantage cost trend and rate-hike macro add caution.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Coin-flip on a threshold set near ~10% growth, roughly UNH's historical long-term EPS growth target low end (~50%).
- **Resolution rule:** YES if the 2027 adjusted EPS outlook first issued (expected with Q4 2026 results, Jan-2027) has a low end or 'at least' floor ≥ $22.50. If issued as a single point, use that point.
- **Resolution source:** UnitedHealth Q4 2026 earnings 8-K (SEC EDGAR, CIK 731766)

- **Headcount:** permanent employees 1,309 + permanent workers 1,779 = **3,088 on rolls**. Contract ("other than permanent") workers 2,057 (FY25: 2,159). Total including contract staff 3,910 `[AR26 Directors' report]`.
- **Minimum wage:** **0% of permanent staff are at minimum wage. 80% of contract workers (1,640) are.**
- **Median pay:** permanent workers (male) ₹10.0 lakh/yr, female ₹7.9 lakh. Employees (male) ₹36.3 lakh, female ₹26.3 lakh. Median remuneration of all employees ₹12.0 lakh. MD = 61× the median.
- **Raises:** non-managerial salaries +13.0%; KMP +29.9%; median +5.55%.
- **Turnover:** permanent employees 7%, workers 4% (VMM: 84%).
- **Minimum-wage pool** [EST]. 1,640 contract workers × ~₹2.3–2.8 lakh/yr all-in agency cost (Maharashtra engineering-industry minimum wage plus a ~29% statutory load and agency margin; the Maharashtra rate was not looked up this session, so unverified) ≈ **₹38–46 cr ≈ 0.3–0.4% of sales**. A 10% minimum-wage revision ≈ **3–4 bps of margin** (VMM: 55–60 bps for a 15% step). **The wage-gazette leading indicator that mattered for the retailer is noise here.**
- **What does matter:** (a) the **labour codes** (₹94.2 cr one-time charge plus a higher recurring gratuity/leave base). Employee cost rose 18% YoY in Q2 FY27 against sales +4% `[Q2R]`, so ~80 bps of margin. (b) The unionised permanent workforce at Kothrud: a retirement-age dispute (58 vs 60) is pending in the Bombay HC; the order is stayed and there is "no material financial impact" `[NSE 12-Jun-2026]`.
- **Productivity:** revenue per permanent employee ₹3.9 cr [EST: 12,143 ÷ 3,088]. KOEL was not computed this session (open).

body:
Pick visits to test the model, not for convenience. Pune is the natural base (plants, the Balewadi HQ, dealers, a large DC cluster nearby in Mumbai/Navi Mumbai). About 2 days.

**Visit A: a GOEM or GOEM-authorised genset dealer** (e.g. a Sudhir Power or Jakson sales office, Pune or Delhi NCR), plus one KOEL and one Mahindra Powerol dealer in the same city.
1. **Price sheet by node:** list and transaction price for 62.5, 125, 250, 500 and 1,010 kVA CPCB IV+ sets, and for a 2,000+ kVA HHP set: Cummins vs KOEL vs Mahindra vs Greaves. Repeat quarterly (the fixed price basket). This tests the "10–15% Cummins premium" (analyst's assertion, not confirmed `[CC-Q2FY27]`) and whether CIL's Q1 FY27 price hike stuck.
2. **Price-hike log:** dates and % of engine vs alternator vs canopy increases since Apr-2026. This tests the claim that "alternator players took most of the hike, engines single-digit" (Macquarie on the call) and gives the pass-through lag directly.
3. **Lead time** today for a QSK60 and a QSK95 set vs a Perkins/Baudouin set. This tests the "allocation" risk (§3.3) and the DC share.
4. **Who are the three big customers?** Ask how the GOEM's volume split between DC, realty and industrial moved. This tests the 31% concentration inference (§2.3).

**Visit B: a Cummins dealer workshop or parts counter (distribution business)**
5. **Count:** service bays, technicians, jobs on the board, share of CPCB IV+ jobs; parts-counter tickets per hour.
6. **Post-warranty CPCB IV+ tickets:** what fails (DPF/SCR, sensors, ECU), parts price per job, and whether customers come back after warranty or go to independent mechanics. This tests the "aftermarket second wave" (§4.2).
7. **Will-fit vs genuine:** price of 5 fixed parts (filters, injector, turbo, gasket kit, starter) genuine vs will-fit vs "OEM second-line". This tests the MD&A threat about will-fit parts and gives a quarterly time series.
8. **Dealer economics:** margin on parts vs gensets (ask in ranges), the royalty paid to CIL (it exists: "royalty income from dealers" `[AR26 n.26]`), technician pay and attrition, and the dealer's view of the 14 new "2S" LHP dealers. Never ask for confidential CIL data.
9. **Retrofit and dual fuel:** monthly enquiries for RECD and DF kits under the CAQM orders (NCR) — a regulation-driven aftermarket.

body:
- **H1 (MD&A change):** firms whose MD&A changed most vs the prior year's report (bottom quintile of MD&A Jaccard
  word-set similarity, within pair-year) underperform sector-and-size-matched controls over 12 months. Sign: negative.
- **H2 (auditor + CARO change):** same with the auditor's report + CARO section (bottom quintile of AUD Jaccard).
  Sign: negative.
- **H3 (auditor-section change flag):** firm-years whose auditor section contains, for the first time vs the
  prior year, an emphasis of matter, a qualified / adverse / disclaimer opinion, a material uncertainty related to
  going concern, an ICFR material weakness, or a CARO adverse clause (default in repayment, cash losses, auditor
  resignation, short-term funds used long-term, CARO going-concern doubt, fraud noticed, undisputed statutory
  dues in arrears > 6 months) underperform controls over 12 months. Detected by keyword-in-sentence without a
  negator ("no", "not", "nil", "none") in the same sentence, current year vs prior year; **every flagged case is
  then checked by hand** (read the sentence); only confirmed new items count. Sign: negative.

FY26 interest on bank deposits ₹19.5 cr + MF gains/fair value ₹7.5 cr `[AR26 n.22]` on an average ~₹330 cr balance ≈ 8% — consistent. ICRA AA-(Stable)/A1+ reaffirmed 02-Feb-2026. |

Materials 67.5% of revenue with back-to-back steel pass-through — normal for a forging/machining axle maker. |
| H1c unverifiable profits | **pass** | Customers are listed OEMs (Customer A ₹1,440 cr = 66% of FY26 revenue `[AR26 n.32]`, almost certainly Ashok Leyland per call questions; Customer B ₹214 cr). Exports to group companies (Cameri, Troy) ₹62 cr. |
| H2 auditor exit / qualified opinion | **pass** | S R Batliboi & Associates LLP (EY), unmodified opinions FY25 and FY26; one KAM (slow-moving inventory provision) `[AR26 p.94]`. CARO 3(xviii) no resignation. Audit-trail exception for direct DB changes (common). Q2 FY27 limited review unmodified. |
| H3 rating not cooperating | **pass** | ICRA AA-(Stable)/A1+ on ₹135 cr, letter 02-Feb-2026 `[ICRA]`. |

| H5 RPT leakage | **pass (watch, see L5)** | Largest RPT is the **technical fee to Meritor HVS (India) Ltd (MHVSIL)** ₹97.5 cr FY26 (4.5% of sales) under an annual services agreement after minority shareholders **rejected** (79.5% against, Dec-2024) a ₹2,500 cr material-RPT resolution with MHVSIL `[AR25 CG report]`. Not leakage on present evidence (OPM rose 10.6% → 10.9% after the switch), but it is the single biggest parent take. |
| Exit triggers | **none** | Results on time; KSPCB notice disclosed 5 days late (09-Aug-2026, reason given). |
| G pledge (v3) | **clear** | NSE pledge API 23-Nov-2026: promoter shares pledged 0 (0.00% of promoter holding); SHP XBRL 30-Sep-2026: all three encumbrance flags false. Promoters 71.04%, unchanged since 2017 `[SCR]`. Cummins Reg 31(4) annual declaration 24-Jul-2026. |
| G accounting trouble (5 y) | **clear** | None. Minor: NSE format query on the Q4 FY21 audit report (resolved 27-May-2021). |
| G dilution | **clear** | 1,51,11,975 shares, unchanged. |
| G solvency set (S1/S5) | **clear** | `solvency_screen.py` 23-Nov-2026: grade blank, 0 flags, ICR 110.5x (FY26). Debt = lease liabilities ₹13 cr only. |
| Q CFO/PAT | ok | FY22–26 CFO ₹656 cr vs PAT ₹722 cr = **0.91x** `[SCR]`; FY25 receivables via MHVSIL ₹387 cr unwound in FY26. |
| Q other-income share | ok | FY26 other income ₹32 cr = 15% of PBT (treasury). |
| Q CARO 3(iii) loans | note | Loans to five **suppliers** (₹5.6 cr, secured on machinery they bought; one ₹0.03 cr overdue >365 days at AB Auto Brakes) `[AR26 n.37]`. Supplier financing to secure capacity — consistent with the "supply-chain constraint" story. |

body:
| source | how | status (tested 25-Nov-2026 from a cloud IP) |
|---|---|---|
| `google_news` | Google News RSS search, one query per company: `"name" OR "alias" OR TICKER when:Nd`. India edition (`hl=en-IN&gl=IN`) for Indian names, US edition for `US-` names | **works**. 90 queries, 3,912 rows over 7 days. One HTTP 429 cleared after the 10 s back-off |
| `ratings_news` | one Google News query: agency names (CRISIL, ICRA, CARE/CareEdge, India Ratings, Acuite, Brickwork, Infomerics) AND action words. Kept only when the headline names a watchlist company. Company items with an agency name in the headline are also tagged `rating` | **works** (50 to 100 rows, 0 matched our names on the first run) |
| `sebi_order`, `sebi_press` | public listing HTML on sebi.gov.in (Enforcement > Orders, `sid=2&ssid=9`; Press releases, `sid=6&ssid=23`), first page of 25 rows each, matched by company name | **works**. The page has a CAPTCHA for the *login* widget only; the listing itself is open. `sebirss.xml` is empty (323 bytes) |
| `rbi_press` | `rbi.org.in/pressreleases_rss.xml`. Items that name a watchlist company go to that company. Lender-policy titles (SFB, microfinance, NBFC, risk weight, monetary penalty, directions) go to every `sector=lender` ticker as `policy:lender` | **works** |
| `policy_news` | Google News, one query per `policy.csv` row (India edition unless the sector starts with `us`) | **works**, but noisy (foreign items, loosely related headlines). The queries are the place to tune |

**Not automated, by rule or because they cannot be fetched politely.** These are listed in every report:
- NCLT/NCLAT: CAPTCHA. Never automated.
- ICRA company search: the page loads a Barracuda/infisecure bot-protection script, and the search route returns 404.
  Single rationale PDFs (`icra.in/Rating/ShowRationalReportFilePdfViewer/<Id>`) still work when fetched by hand.
- CRISIL rating-rationale listing: the page embeds reCAPTCHA, so its listing JSON is not used. Single rationale HTML pages still work by hand.
- CARE Ratings (JS-heavy, no clean endpoint) and India Ratings (JS single-page app).
- SEBI rows beyond the newest 25 per list: older rows need the site's AJAX pager. A `--since` window longer than about a
  week can therefore miss SEBI rows.
- Exchange "Credit Rating" announcements are already covered by `tools/detectors` (`rating_downgrade`, `rating_not_cooperating`).

Anti-bot handling: a response with a Cloudflare challenge, a Google "unusual traffic" page, reCAPTCHA or hCaptcha
markers is treated as blocked. That host is then skipped for the rest of the run and noted in the report. The CAPTCHA is
never solved or bypassed. A 429 that persists after the back-off also stops that host for the run.

Politeness: one request at a time, at least 3 s between Google requests and 2 s for other hosts, and a 10 s then 20 s
back-off on 429/5xx. A full run is about 110 requests and takes about 5.5 min.
